An automobile with projected area 2.6 $m^{2}$ is running on a road with a speed of 120 km per hour. The mass density and the kinematic viscosity of air are 1.2 $kg/m^{3}$ and $1.5 \times 10^{-5} m^{2}/s$, respectively. The drag coefficient is 0.30.

The metric horse power required to overcome the drag force is

primary.subtopicLabel: Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift
detailed_solution.markdown:
Power required to overcome the drag = Drag force $\times$ velocity

$$\begin{aligned} &=520 \times \frac{120 \times 1000}{60 \times 60}= 17333.33 \mathrm{watt} \\ &\quad (1 \mathrm{mhp}=735.5 \mathrm{watt})\\ &=\frac{17333.33}{735.5}\text{ metric horse power }\\ &=23.567 \text{ metric horse power} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2008:q84.title: GATE CE 2008 | Set 1 | Question: 84
pp:ce:2008:q84.question:
A horizontal curvature curve with a centre line radius of 200 m is provided on a 2-lane, 2-way SH section. The width of the 2-lane road is 7.0 m. Design speed for this section is 80 km per hour. The brake reaction time is 2.4 s, and the coefficients of friction in longitudinal and lateral directions are 0.355 and 0.15, respectively.

The safe stopping sight distance on the section is

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
Safe stopping sight distance

$$\begin{aligned} &=0.278 \mathrm{Vt}+\frac{v^{2}}{254 \mathrm{f}} \\ &=(0.278 \times 80 \times 2.4)+\frac{(80)^{2}}{254 \times 0.355} \\ &=124.35 \mathrm{m} \approx 125 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

A horizontal curvature curve with a centre line radius of 200 m is provided on a 2-lane, 2-way SH section. The width of the 2-lane road is 7.0 m. Design speed for this section is 80 km per hour. The brake reaction time is 2.4 s, and the coefficients of friction in longitudinal and lateral directions are 0.355 and 0.15, respectively.

The set-back distance from the centre line of the inner lane is

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned} m &=(R-d)-(R-d) \cos \frac{\alpha}{2} \\ \frac{\alpha}{2} &=\frac{180 S}{2 \pi(R-d)} \\ &=\frac{180 \times 125}{2 \times \pi\left(200-\frac{7}{4}\right)}=18.063 \\ \therefore \quad m &=200-\left(200-\frac{7}{4}\right) \cos (18.063) \\ &=11.52 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

Thus, set back distance from centre line of inner lane

$=11.52-\left(\frac{7}{4}\right)=9.77 \mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.
